verdict.why: Every still is legible and information-dense: the finished extraction output with per-field confidence and grounding counts is on screen from the first frame, and the motion of the scan band sweeping across the page makes the extraction feel live rather than a static screenshot. A muted viewer can follow the full arc — extract, recover faded ink, quarantine the unreadable, prove the judge fails mutants, all gates passed — because each beat states its claim and its measured number.
fixes: Crop out or shorten the persistent chrome ("agent-next sandbox · disposable · seed 42") — at phone width it is the only unreadable text and it says nothing.
Give the 3.33 s still a one-line "what this is" claim in the frame itself (e.g. "extract invoice fields, or say NO_TEXT") so the payoff is self-explaining before reading the captions.
Hold the "4/4 fields grounded" and the ALL GATES PASSED beats about 1 s longer; the cutoff at 23.33 s / 26.67 s reads as a clip rather than a resolved ending.
Raise the caption type size or move the bottom captions to the top third so they are not competing with the dark panels for contrast.
Add a visible progress/segment indicator (e.g. "1/6 · field accuracy") so the sequence of claims reads as a checklist rather than a reel of screens.
